verdict.rationale: Smithery's Uplink feature is documented as exposing an MCP server running on any machine as a regular Smithery connection. Its stated use cases include testing a server against a real agent before publishing and running a private tool without hosting it, which directly matches bridging a local server as a managed connection without deploying it. missing for 10: documentation of Uplink setup and mechanics (CLI command, tunnel/auth behavior, connection lifecycle and limits), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bridge a locally running MCP server into the platform as a managed remote connection without deploying it

citations.quote: Uplink exposes an MCP server running on any machine as a regular Smithery connection.
You’re developing an MCP server and want to test it against a real agent before publishing.
You want to run a private tool for yourself or your team without hosting it.
